encounters.cc: Four months of progressively infrequent, difficult bowel movements with bloating

lines: Four months of progressively infrequent, difficult bowel movements with bloating

The patient returns to the Endocrinology clinic for follow-up of his longitudinal diabetes care, having previously presented to Gastroenterology in 2020 for nocturnal heartburn and regurgitation and to Pulmonology in early 2021 for episodic facial flushing and itching.
He now reports four months of progressively infrequent, difficult bowel movements with associated bloating.
He states that stools are small, dry, and require straining despite increased water intake.
He denies rectal bleeding, weight loss, or nocturnal pain.
He eats irregularly because he often feels full after just a few bites and sometimes experiences mild nausea after meals.
He notices large glucose swings hours after dinner, even when he eats very little.
He denies recent travel or antibiotic exposure.
He reports that fiber supplements worsened his distension without improving stool frequency.
He denies abdominal pain localized to the right lower quadrant or epigastrium.
He denies greasy stools or oily residue in the toilet.
He reports long-standing diabetes complicated by numbness in his feet, erectile difficulties, and occasional lightheadedness when standing quickly.
Colon cancer screening last year was normal.
- Percutaneous coronary intervention with drug-eluting stent placement (inferior wall)
He takes metformin and basal-bolus insulin; he denies opioid or anticholinergic use.
- Insulin glargine 24 units subcutaneous at bedtime
- Insulin lispro sliding scale with meals
Simvastatin (interstitial lung disease), Niacin (severe flushing and pruritus)
Smoking: Current smoker, 1 pack per day (30 pack-year history).
Orthostatic vitals show a small drop in systolic pressure without compensatory tachycardia.
Physical exam shows dry mucous membranes and a mildly distended, tympanic abdomen with decreased bowel sounds but no tenderness.
Digital rectal exam shows normal tone and no palpable masses or fissures.
There is diminished pinprick sensation in a stocking distribution of both feet.
A plain abdominal film shows moderate stool burden without obstruction.

lines: Acute onset of excessive salivation, lacrimation, and difficulty breathing after spraying insecticides

This 58-year-old male with coronary artery disease, diabetic autonomic neuropathy, and GERD (prior angina and constipation evaluations) presents to the emergency department with his wife, who reports that he has been experiencing excessive salivation, lacrimation, and difficulty breathing over the past hour.
He was spraying insecticides in the field earlier in the day.
- Percutaneous coronary intervention with drug-eluting stent placement (inferior wall)
- Insulin glargine 24 units subcutaneous at bedtime
- Insulin lispro sliding scale with meals
Simvastatin (interstitial lung disease), Niacin (severe flushing and pruritus)
Smoking: Current smoker, 1 pack per day (30 pack-year history).
His vital signs are as follows: blood pressure 90/60 mmHg, heart rate 55 bpm, respiratory rate 28 breaths/min, and oxygen saturation 88% on room air.
On examination, the patient is anxious, diaphoretic, and has miosis.
Auscultation of the lungs reveals bilateral wheezes.
The patient also exhibits muscle fasciculations and weakness.

lines: Severe, pressure-like substernal chest pain radiating to the left shoulder
This 60-year-old male has Coronary Artery Disease and prior inferior wall STEMI in July 2024.
He presents to the emergency department with 90 minutes of severe, pressure-like substernal chest pain radiating to his left shoulder.
- Acute ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) of inferior wall (diagnosed 2024-07-15)
He has a history of hyperlipidemia and type 2 diabetes mellitus.
- Percutaneous coronary intervention with drug-eluting stent placement (inferior wall)
- Insulin glargine 24 units subcutaneous at bedtime
- Insulin lispro sliding scale with meals
Simvastatin (interstitial lung disease), Niacin (severe flushing and pruritus)
He smokes one pack of cigarettes daily and drinks alcohol occasionally.
His temperature is 37.2°C (99°F), blood pressure is 92/60 mm Hg.
He appears diaphoretic and mildly short of breath.
Cardiopulmonary exam reveals clear lung fields and bradycardia.
Cardiac auscultation reveals normal S1 and S2 with no murmurs.
